newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: European gold price higher, seen seeking new range.
newsitem.headline: European gold price higher, seen seeking new range.

text.p: Gold opened firmer in Europe on Monday and traders said the metal was expected to test the upside, propelled by U.S. and European buying to cover short positions taken last week.
Gold started at $327.95/328.35 an ounce after closing in London at $323.90/324.40 on Friday.
Traders said the market was expected to try and break through resistance at $330.
If the move succeeded, gold was expected to settle in a new range of $325/335.
Silver was barely changed at $4.30/4.32 versus $4.29/4.31. The underlying tendency was firmer on the tail of gold, which drew the main activity in precious metals.
Platinum added four dollars to $410.00/413.00 from $406.00/409.00.
Palladium was also firmer at $186.00/189.00 versus $183.50/186.50.
